statement: The analysis includes 14,767 paper records, not 14,767 independent benchmark families.
caveat: Selection error and family duplication are not fully quantified; counts do not measure adoption.

statement: LLM scoring rises from 433/1,681 (25.8%) to 2,309/5,734 (40.3%) in the matched January-August windows.
caveat: These are coded design shares, not changes in scoring reliability.

statement: Of the 14.51 percentage-point increase, agent composition contributes 0.56 and within-group change 13.95.
caveat: A symmetric arithmetic allocation under this grouping, not a causal effect.

statement: Across the full window, 3,272/14,763 (22.2%) combine generated materials with LLM scoring.
caveat: Different roles can involve different models, components or evaluation stages.

statement: Within this intersection, 2,530/3,272 (77.3%) also use human/real-world materials and 2,020/3,272 (61.7%) additional scoring mechanisms.
caveat: These categories overlap; mixed design does not establish oversight or quality.

statement: Joint prevalence increases, but lift changes from 1.32 to 1.22; an increasingly strong association is not established.
caveat: Association strength is distinct from changes in the two marginal shares.
Language coverage is a secondary result; absent tags do not prove unsupported languages.
